bio: Hi! I'm Samrat Kumar Dey, currently pursuing my PhD in Informatics with a specialization in Medical Informatics at the University of Missouri-Columbia. Alongside my doctoral studies, I work as a Graduate Research Assistant at the MU Institute for Data Science and Informatics in the Interdisciplinary Data Analytics and Search (iDAS) Lab under the guidance of Prof. Dr. Chi-Ren Shyu.

My work sits at the intersection of clinical data and machine learning: building and evaluating models that turn messy real-world health data — electronic health records, medical images, physiological signals and epidemiological surveillance — into decisions clinicians and public-health teams can actually act on. Before starting my doctorate I spent a decade teaching computer science in Bangladesh, and I still care deeply about making technical work legible to the people who have to use it.
I strongly resonate with the words of the famous American baseball player Babe Ruth, who said, "It's hard to beat a person who never gives up."
